For this assessment each working group's task is to design and validate a new attitude questionnaire and to present your findings using a digital academic poster.



























The topic of the attitude questionnaire will be chosen by your group but must be approved by the teaching team before you collect any data.



























For the poster presentation, your group's task is to create an engaging, scientifically sound and informative poster about the attitude scale you will have designed and validated.

What is your scale? Why is it needed? (i.e. what contribution does it make to what is known about your attitude object?)













Is it reliable?













Is it valid?













What does it show about the construct/attitude object?













How could we use it?













Further materials and guidance to help you construct your poster are available on Canvas and will be added to through the Assessment Support Tasks.



























The aim of this assessment is to allow you to develop your skills at presenting complex information concisely and in a visually engaging format. It also provides you with an opportunity to receive feedback on your poster presentation skills in preparation for your final year project poster conference.

The group grade will be decided by two markers from the RMD teaching team. The first marker will mark the poster in advance of the online viva and will lead the questions about the poster. Their mark will - once moderated - form the basis of your group assignment mark.  They can use the online viva to improve on or confirm your poster mark (but you cannot reduce your mark at this point). The second marker, who will attend the online viva, will also ask questions and will also provide feedback on your poster. The first and second markers will agree a group grade.

tasks_other1:
For this assessment each working group's task is to design and validate a new attitude questionnaire and to present your findings using a digital academic poster.



























The topic of the attitude questionnaire will be chosen by your group but must be approved by the teaching team before you collect any data.



























For the poster presentation, your group's task is to create an engaging, scientifically sound and informative poster about the attitude scale you will have designed and validated.



























The scale validation process should answer the following questions about your scale:



























What is your scale? Why is it needed? (i.e. what contribution does it make to what is known about your attitude object?)













Is it reliable?













Is it valid?













What does it show about the construct/attitude object?













How could we use it?













Further materials and guidance to help you construct your poster are available on Canvas and will be added to through the Assessment Support Tasks.



























The aim of this assessment is to allow you to develop your skills at presenting complex information concisely and in a visually engaging format. This involves the clear communication of detailed and complex information by selecting the most relevant details and presenting these on a poster that can stand alone, but that you are also able to expand upon in a discussion about your poster.



























It also provides you with an opportunity to receive feedback on your poster presentation skills in preparation for your final year project poster conference.
info_other1:
For the group online viva of the poster you should be prepared to engage in discussion about your poster for 10 minutes. 













The group grade will be decided by two markers from the RMD teaching team. The first marker will mark the poster in advance of the online viva and will lead the questions about the poster. Their mark will - once moderated - form the basis of your group assignment mark.  They can use the online viva to improve on or confirm your poster mark (but you cannot reduce your mark at this point). The second marker, who will attend the online viva, will also ask questions and will also provide feedback on your poster. The first and second markers will agree a group grade.

For this assessment each working group's task is to design and validate a new attitude questionnaire and to present your findings using a digital academic poster.



























The topic of the attitude questionnaire will be chosen by your group but must be approved by the teaching team before you collect any data.



























For the poster presentation, your group's task is to create an engaging, scientifically sound and informative poster about the attitude scale you will have designed and validated.



























The scale validation process should answer the following questions about your scale:



























What is your scale? Why is it needed? (i.e. what contribution does it make to what is known about your attitude object?)













Is it reliable?













Is it valid?













What does it show about the construct/attitude object?













How could we use it?













Further materials and guidance to help you construct your poster are available on Canvas and will be added to through the Assessment Support Tasks.



























The aim of this assessment is to allow you to develop your skills at presenting complex information concisely and in a visually engaging format. This involves the clear communication of detailed and complex information by selecting the most relevant details and presenting these on a poster that can stand alone, but that you are also able to expand upon in a discussion about your poster.



























It also provides you with an opportunity to receive feedback on your poster presentation skills in preparation for your final year project poster conference.
info_other1:
For the group online viva of the poster you should be prepared to engage in discussion about your poster for 10 minutes. 













The group grade will be decided by two markers from the RMD teaching team. The first marker will mark the poster in advance of the online viva and will lead the questions about the poster. Their mark will - once moderated - form the basis of your group assignment mark.  They can use the online viva to improve on or confirm your poster mark (but you cannot reduce your mark at this point). The second marker, who will attend the online viva, will also ask questions and will also provide feedback on your poster. The first and second markers will agree a group grade.

For this assessment each working group's task is to design and validate a new attitude questionnaire and to present your findings using a digital academic poster.



























The topic of the attitude questionnaire will be chosen by your group but must be approved by the teaching team before you collect any data.



























For the poster presentation, your group's task is to create an engaging, scientifically sound and informative poster about the attitude scale you will have designed and validated.



























The scale validation process should answer the following questions about your scale:



























What is your scale? Why is it needed? (i.e. what contribution does it make to what is known about your attitude object?)













Is it reliable?













Is it valid?













What does it show about the construct/attitude object?













How could we use it?













Further materials and guidance to help you construct your poster are available on Canvas and will be added to through the Assessment Support Tasks.



























The aim of this assessment is to allow you to develop your skills at presenting complex information concisely and in a visually engaging format. This involves the clear communication of detailed and complex information by selecting the most relevant details and presenting these on a poster that can stand alone, but that you are also able to expand upon in a discussion about your poster.



























It also provides you with an opportunity to receive feedback on your poster presentation skills in preparation for your final year project poster conference.
info_other1:

The second marker, who will attend the online viva, will also ask questions and will also provide feedback on your poster. The first and second markers will agree a group grade.

For this assessment each working group's task is to design and validate a new attitude questionnaire and to present your findings using a digital academic poster.



























The topic of the attitude questionnaire will be chosen by your group but must be approved by the teaching team before you collect any data.



























For the poster presentation, your group's task is to create an engaging, scientifically sound and informative poster about the attitude scale you will have designed and validated.



























The scale validation process should answer the following questions about your scale:



























What is your scale? Why is it needed? (i.e. what contribution does it make to what is known about your attitude object?)













Is it reliable?













Is it valid?













What does it show about the construct/attitude object?













How could we use it?













Further materials and guidance to help you construct your poster are available on Canvas and will be added to through the Assessment Support Tasks.



























The aim of this assessment is to allow you to develop your skills at presenting complex information concisely and in a visually engaging format. This involves the clear communication of detailed and complex information by selecting the most relevant details and presenting these on a poster that can stand alone, but that you are also able to expand upon in a discussion about your poster.



























It also provides you with an opportunity to receive feedback on your poster presentation skills in preparation for your final year project poster conference.
info_other1:
For the group online viva of the poster you should be prepared to engage in discussion about your poster for 10 minutes. 













The group grade will be decided by two markers from the RMD teaching team. The first marker will mark the poster in advance of the online viva and will lead the questions about the poster. Their mark will - once moderated - form the basis of your group assignment mark.  They can use the online viva to improve on or confirm your poster mark (but you cannot reduce your mark at this point). The second marker, who will attend the online viva, will also ask questions and will also provide feedback on your poster. The first and second markers will agree a group grade.

tasks_other1:
For this assessment each working group's task is to design and validate a new attitude questionnaire and to present your findings using a digital academic poster.



























The topic of the attitude questionnaire will be chosen by your group but must be approved by the teaching team before you collect any data.



























For the poster presentation, your group's task is to create an engaging, scientifically sound and informative poster about the attitude scale you will have designed and validated.



























The scale validation process should answer the following questions about your scale:



























What is your scale? Why is it needed? (i.e. what contribution does it make to what is known about your attitude object?)













Is it reliable?













Is it valid?













What does it show about the construct/attitude object?













How could we use it?













Further materials and guidance to help you construct your poster are available on Canvas and will be added to through the Assessment Support Tasks.



























The aim of this assessment is to allow you to develop your skills at presenting complex information concisely and in a visually engaging format. This involves the clear communication of detailed and complex information by selecting the most relevant details and presenting these on a poster that can stand alone, but that you are also able to expand upon in a discussion about your poster.



























It also provides you with an opportunity to receive feedback on your poster presentation skills in preparation for your final year project poster conference.
info_other1:
For the group online viva of the poster you should be prepared to engage in discussion about your poster for 10 minutes. 













The group grade will be decided by two markers from the RMD teaching team. The first marker will mark the poster in advance of the online viva and will lead the questions about the poster. Their mark will - once moderated - form the basis of your group assignment mark.  They can use the online viva to improve on or confirm your poster mark (but you cannot reduce your mark at this point). The second marker, who will attend the online viva, will also ask questions and will also provide feedback on your poster. The first and second markers will agree a group grade.

tasks_other1:
For this assessment each working group's task is to design and validate a new attitude questionnaire and to present your findings using a digital academic poster.



























The topic of the attitude questionnaire will be chosen by your group but must be approved by the teaching team before you collect any data.



























For the poster presentation, your group's task is to create an engaging, scientifically sound and informative poster about the attitude scale you will have designed and validated.



























The scale validation process should answer the following questions about your scale:



























What is your scale? Why is it needed? (i.e. what contribution does it make to what is known about your attitude object?)













Is it reliable?













Is it valid?













What does it show about the construct/attitude object?













How could we use it?













Further materials and guidance to help you construct your poster are available on Canvas and will be added to through the Assessment Support Tasks.



























The aim of this assessment is to allow you to develop your skills at presenting complex information concisely and in a visually engaging format. This involves the clear communication of detailed and complex information by selecting the most relevant details and presenting these on a poster that can stand alone, but that you are also able to expand upon in a discussion about your poster.



























It also provides you with an opportunity to receive feedback on your poster presentation skills in preparation for your final year project poster conference.
info_other1:
For the group online viva of the poster you should be prepared to engage in discussion about your poster for 10 minutes. 













The group grade will be decided by two markers from the RMD teaching team. The first marker will mark the poster in advance of the online viva and will lead the questions about the poster. Their mark will - once moderated - form the basis of your group assignment mark.  They can use the online viva to improve on or confirm your poster mark (but you cannot reduce your mark at this point). The second marker, who will attend the online viva, will also ask questions and will also provide feedback on your poster. The first and second markers will agree a group grade.

How could we use it?

For this assessment each working group's task is to design and validate a new attitude questionnaire and to present your findings using a digital academic poster.



























The topic of the attitude questionnaire will be chosen by your group but must be approved by the teaching team before you collect any data.



























For the poster presentation, your group's task is to create an engaging, scientifically sound and informative poster about the attitude scale you will have designed and validated.



























The scale validation process should answer the following questions about your scale:



























What is your scale? Why is it needed? (i.e. what contribution does it make to what is known about your attitude object?)













Is it reliable?













Is it valid?













What does it show about the construct/attitude object?













How could we use it?













Further materials and guidance to help you construct your poster are available on Canvas and will be added to through the Assessment Support Tasks.



























The aim of this assessment is to allow you to develop your skills at presenting complex information concisely and in a visually engaging format. This involves the clear communication of detailed and complex information by selecting the most relevant details and presenting these on a poster that can stand alone, but that you are also able to expand upon in a discussion about your poster.



























It also provides you with an opportunity to receive feedback on your poster presentation skills in preparation for your final year project poster conference.
info_other1:
For the group online viva of the poster you should be prepared to engage in discussion about your poster for 10 minutes. 













The group grade will be decided by two markers from the RMD teaching team. The first marker will mark the poster in advance of the online viva and will lead the questions about the poster. Their mark will - once moderated - form the basis of your group assignment mark.  They can use the online viva to improve on or confirm your poster mark (but you cannot reduce your mark at this point). The second marker, who will attend the online viva, will also ask questions and will also provide feedback on your poster. The first and second markers will agree a group grade.

tasks_other1:
For this assessment each working group's task is to design and validate a new attitude questionnaire and to present your findings using a digital academic poster.



























The topic of the attitude questionnaire will be chosen by your group but must be approved by the teaching team before you collect any data.



























For the poster presentation, your group's task is to create an engaging, scientifically sound and informative poster about the attitude scale you will have designed and validated.



























The scale validation process should answer the following questions about your scale:



























What is your scale? Why is it needed? (i.e. what contribution does it make to what is known about your attitude object?)













Is it reliable?













Is it valid?













What does it show about the construct/attitude object?













How could we use it?













Further materials and guidance to help you construct your poster are available on Canvas and will be added to through the Assessment Support Tasks.



























The aim of this assessment is to allow you to develop your skills at presenting complex information concisely and in a visually engaging format. This involves the clear communication of detailed and complex information by selecting the most relevant details and presenting these on a poster that can stand alone, but that you are also able to expand upon in a discussion about your poster.



























It also provides you with an opportunity to receive feedback on your poster presentation skills in preparation for your final year project poster conference.
info_other1:
For the group online viva of the poster you should be prepared to engage in discussion about your poster for 10 minutes. 













The group grade will be decided by two markers from the RMD teaching team. The first marker will mark the poster in advance of the online viva and will lead the questions about the poster. Their mark will - once moderated - form the basis of your group assignment mark.  They can use the online viva to improve on or confirm your poster mark (but you cannot reduce your mark at this point). The second marker, who will attend the online viva, will also ask questions and will also provide feedback on your poster. The first and second markers will agree a group grade.

For this assessment each working group's task is to design and validate a new attitude questionnaire and to present your findings using a digital academic poster.



























The topic of the attitude questionnaire will be chosen by your group but must be approved by the teaching team before you collect any data.



























For the poster presentation, your group's task is to create an engaging, scientifically sound and informative poster about the attitude scale you will have designed and validated.



























The scale validation process should answer the following questions about your scale:



























What is your scale? Why is it needed? (i.e. what contribution does it make to what is known about your attitude object?)













Is it reliable?













Is it valid?













What does it show about the construct/attitude object?













How could we use it?













Further materials and guidance to help you construct your poster are available on Canvas and will be added to through the Assessment Support Tasks.



























The aim of this assessment is to allow you to develop your skills at presenting complex information concisely and in a visually engaging format. This involves the clear communication of detailed and complex information by selecting the most relevant details and presenting these on a poster that can stand alone, but that you are also able to expand upon in a discussion about your poster.



























It also provides you with an opportunity to receive feedback on your poster presentation skills in preparation for your final year project poster conference.

Their mark will - once moderated - form the basis of your group assignment mark.  They can use the online viva to improve on or confirm your poster mark (but you cannot reduce your mark at this point). The second marker, who will attend the online viva, will also ask questions and will also provide feedback on your poster. The first and second markers will agree a group grade.

tasks_other1:
For this assessment each working group's task is to design and validate a new attitude questionnaire and to present your findings using a digital academic poster.



























The topic of the attitude questionnaire will be chosen by your group but must be approved by the teaching team before you collect any data.



























For the poster presentation, your group's task is to create an engaging, scientifically sound and informative poster about the attitude scale you will have designed and validated.



























The scale validation process should answer the following questions about your scale:



























What is your scale? Why is it needed? (i.e. what contribution does it make to what is known about your attitude object?)













Is it reliable?













Is it valid?













What does it show about the construct/attitude object?













How could we use it?













Further materials and guidance to help you construct your poster are available on Canvas and will be added to through the Assessment Support Tasks.



























The aim of this assessment is to allow you to develop your skills at presenting complex information concisely and in a visually engaging format. This involves the clear communication of detailed and complex information by selecting the most relevant details and presenting these on a poster that can stand alone, but that you are also able to expand upon in a discussion about your poster.



























It also provides you with an opportunity to receive feedback on your poster presentation skills in preparation for your final year project poster conference.
info_other1:
For the group online viva of the poster you should be prepared to engage in discussion about your poster for 10 minutes. 













The group grade will be decided by two markers from the RMD teaching team. The first marker will mark the poster in advance of the online viva and will lead the questions about the poster. Their mark will - once moderated - form the basis of your group assignment mark.  They can use the online viva to improve on or confirm your poster mark (but you cannot reduce your mark at this point). The second marker, who will attend the online viva, will also ask questions and will also provide feedback on your poster. The first and second markers will agree a group grade.

For this assessment each working group's task is to design and validate a new attitude questionnaire and to present your findings using a digital academic poster.



























The topic of the attitude questionnaire will be chosen by your group but must be approved by the teaching team before you collect any data.



























For the poster presentation, your group's task is to create an engaging, scientifically sound and informative poster about the attitude scale you will have designed and validated.



























The scale validation process should answer the following questions about your scale:



























What is your scale? Why is it needed? (i.e. what contribution does it make to what is known about your attitude object?)













Is it reliable?













Is it valid?













What does it show about the construct/attitude object?













How could we use it?













Further materials and guidance to help you construct your poster are available on Canvas and will be added to through the Assessment Support Tasks.



























The aim of this assessment is to allow you to develop your skills at presenting complex information concisely and in a visually engaging format. This involves the clear communication of detailed and complex information by selecting the most relevant details and presenting these on a poster that can stand alone, but that you are also able to expand upon in a discussion about your poster.



























It also provides you with an opportunity to receive feedback on your poster presentation skills in preparation for your final year project poster conference.
info_other1:
For the group online viva of the poster you should be prepared to engage in discussion about your poster for 10 minutes. 













The group grade will be decided by two markers from the RMD teaching team. The first marker will mark the poster in advance of the online viva and will lead the questions about the poster. Their mark will - once moderated - form the basis of your group assignment mark.  They can use the online viva to improve on or confirm your poster mark (but you cannot reduce your mark at this point). The second marker, who will attend the online viva, will also ask questions and will also provide feedback on your poster. The first and second markers will agree a group grade.

tasks_other1:
For this assessment each working group's task is to design and validate a new attitude questionnaire and to present your findings using a digital academic poster.



























The topic of the attitude questionnaire will be chosen by your group but must be approved by the teaching team before you collect any data.



























For the poster presentation, your group's task is to create an engaging, scientifically sound and informative poster about the attitude scale you will have designed and validated.



























The scale validation process should answer the following questions about your scale:



























What is your scale? Why is it needed? (i.e. what contribution does it make to what is known about your attitude object?)













Is it reliable?













Is it valid?













What does it show about the construct/attitude object?













How could we use it?













Further materials and guidance to help you construct your poster are available on Canvas and will be added to through the Assessment Support Tasks.



























The aim of this assessment is to allow you to develop your skills at presenting complex information concisely and in a visually engaging format. This involves the clear communication of detailed and complex information by selecting the most relevant details and presenting these on a poster that can stand alone, but that you are also able to expand upon in a discussion about your poster.



























It also provides you with an opportunity to receive feedback on your poster presentation skills in preparation for your final year project poster conference.
info_other1:
For the group online viva of the poster you should be prepared to engage in discussion about your poster for 10 minutes. 













The group grade will be decided by two markers from the RMD teaching team. The first marker will mark the poster in advance of the online viva and will lead the questions about the poster. Their mark will - once moderated - form the basis of your group assignment mark.  They can use the online viva to improve on or confirm your poster mark (but you cannot reduce your mark at this point). The second marker, who will attend the online viva, will also ask questions and will also provide feedback on your poster. The first and second markers will agree a group grade.

For this assessment each working group's task is to design and validate a new attitude questionnaire and to present your findings using a digital academic poster.



























The topic of the attitude questionnaire will be chosen by your group but must be approved by the teaching team before you collect any data.



























For the poster presentation, your group's task is to create an engaging, scientifically sound and informative poster about the attitude scale you will have designed and validated.



























The scale validation process should answer the following questions about your scale:



























What is your scale? Why is it needed? (i.e. what contribution does it make to what is known about your attitude object?)













Is it reliable?













Is it valid?













What does it show about the construct/attitude object?













How could we use it?













Further materials and guidance to help you construct your poster are available on Canvas and will be added to through the Assessment Support Tasks.



























The aim of this assessment is to allow you to develop your skills at presenting complex information concisely and in a visually engaging format. This involves the clear communication of detailed and complex information by selecting the most relevant details and presenting these on a poster that can stand alone, but that you are also able to expand upon in a discussion about your poster.



























It also provides you with an opportunity to receive feedback on your poster presentation skills in preparation for your final year project poster conference.
info_other1:
For the group online viva of the poster you should be prepared to engage in discussion about your poster for 10 minutes. 













The group grade will be decided by two markers from the RMD teaching team. The first marker will mark the poster in advance of the online viva and will lead the questions about the poster. Their mark will - once moderated - form the basis of your group assignment mark.  They can use the online viva to improve on or confirm your poster mark (but you cannot reduce your mark at this point). The second marker, who will attend the online viva, will also ask questions and will also provide feedback on your poster. The first and second markers will agree a group grade.
